prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1453; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give a recorded statement today. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my name on the recording, if that's okay. I'm the driver of the vehicle that was struck.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where and when the collision happened?

A: It was on a weekday afternoon in Pearland, Texas, on a main road near a shopping center. I was stopped at a red light in the right lane.

Q: What happened next?

A: The car behind me didn't stop in time. I felt a hard jolt from behind and my head snapped back against the headrest.

Q: Did you exchange information with the other driver?

A: Yes. We swapped insurance and contact details. The other driver said they looked down at their phone for a second.

Q: Did the police respond to the scene?

A: An officer came out and took a report. I think it's on file, but I didn't get a copy yet.

Q: How are you feeling physically?

A: My lower back has been sore since then, and the pain gets worse when I sit for a long time. I saw a doctor the next day and was told I have a back strain. I've been doing physical therapy twice a week.

Q: Were you able to drive your car afterward?

A: The car was drivable, but the rear bumper is damaged and the trunk doesn't latch right. I've been using a rental since then.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?

A: A few days, yes. I'm back to work now, but I'm limited on lifting and I need to stand up and move around often.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I want to cooperate fully and get my car repaired. Thank you.
